 Moussa Diabaté piled up 12 points (5-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds, two assists and three blocks over 26 minutes in a loss to the Clippers on Sunday. 
 Diabaté drew the starting assignment over Ryan Kalkbrenner for the second consecutive contest and delivered his third double-double of the season. It was his highest scoring output since a 17-point outburst against the Nets back on opening night. He’s a strong source of rebounds for fantasy purposes and he’s also averaging two blocks per-game over the last week. The Hornets are in line for a two-game week that features road matchups against the Lakers and Hawks.

 Moussa Diabaté (quad) is probable for Thursday’s game against the Suns. 
 Diabaté is on track to play Thursday night after missing the Hornets’ last two games with a quad injury. If so, his return would bump Ryan Kalkbrenner to the bench. 
 Ryan Kalkbrenner 
 CHA 
 Center 
 #11 
 Ryan Kalkbrenner tallied eight points (4-of-7 FGs), 15 rebounds, three assists, two steals and three blocks in Monday’s win over the Cavaliers. 
 Despite the low point total, Kalkbrenner was dominant on Monday night. Ten of his 15 rebounds came on the offensive end of the floor, and those extra opportunities helped the Hornets put up 124 points. The 7-foot-1 center, once again starting for the injured Moussa Diabaté, also recorded three assists and five defensive contributions. Kalkbrenner is worth rostering as long as the Hornets are without Diabaté.

 Naz Reid (nose) accounted for 23 points (8-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds, four assists, two steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers.
 The line Reid recorded against the Lakers was in line with what many fantasy managers hoped to see from him consistently in Charlotte. Unfortunately, things haven’t worked out that way, and Tuesday’s overtime loss dropped the Hornets to 4-10. Making matters worse for Reid was an inadvertent elbow from Collin Sexton that he took to the nose late in overtime. He was subbed out and did not return. With Coby White and Brandon Miller shut down at the end of regulation, the Hornets lacked the options needed to potentially force a second overtime. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Coby White

 Coby White finished Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers with 19 points (6-of-12 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, three steals and two three-pointers.
 Although White has played in each of Charlotte’s last seven games, the team continues to limit his minutes. He logged 26 minutes on Tuesday and, along with Brandon Miller, did not play at all in overtime. The injuries and minutes restrictions the Hornets have dealt with have a lot to do with them being the worst fourth-quarter team in the NBA this season. Down the stretch on Tuesday, White and the other Hornets failed to do much offensively, with even inbounding the ball becoming an adventure. Charlotte doesn’t play again until Friday, which may be a good thing for White.

 Kevon Looney finished Tuesday’s loss to the Hornets with four points (2-of-3 FGs) and seven rebounds.
 With Walker Kessler (leg) out, the Lakers turned to Looney to start at center on Tuesday. While the veteran center grabbed seven rebounds, he played only 17 minutes, and his mobility was an issue. With Sandro Mamukelashvili (3/3/2/1) shooting 1-of-8 from the field, Lakers head coach JJ Redick eventually turned to two-way contract player Carson Cooper. While his numbers (3/4/2 in 18 minutes) won’t jump off the page, Cooper’s contributions as a rebounder and defender were one reason why the Lakers were able to rally. Kessler is expected to be available for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz, so Looney may find himself out of the rotation once again. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Luka Dončić tallied 36 points (13-of-34 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets.
 Dončić didn’t have a great night shooting-wise, going 5-of-16 from three, but he still posted a complete stat line. The Lakers’ star has scored at least 32 points in 11 straight appearances, with the Lakers going 9-2 in those games. With Tuesday’s overtime win, the Lakers boast the best record in the Western Conference, something few expected at any point this season. Dončić has played like an MVP so far, whether the conversation is focused on the “actual” basketball or the fantasy basketball. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Quentin Grimes 
 LAL 
 Guard

 Player Stats

 Quentin Grimes amassed 47 points (16-of-24 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, one steal and 10 three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets.
 Grimes had the best game of his career on Tuesday, and the Lakers needed it, trailing by as much as 18 late in the third quarter before rallying to win in overtime. Grimes scored 21 points in the fourth quarter alone, outscoring the Hornets by four, and his three-pointer with 1.7 seconds left forced overtime. Austin Reaves (heel) is supposed to test his injured heel on Wednesday before that night’s game against the Jazz, so we should learn more about how much time he’ll miss. Grimes, the first Laker other than Reaves, Luka Dončić or LeBron James to record a 30-point game since Dalton Knecht did in March 2025, will start as long as Reaves is out, and he’s worth rostering until that changes. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Darius Garland accumulated 20 points (5-of-15 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), three rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Jazz.
 While Garland kept the turnovers in check, committing one, and recorded a full stat line, he had a tough night shooting the basketball. The Clippers guard was 5-of-15 from the field, a far cry from his 50.6 percent shooting for the season. The biggest concern for him in fantasy basketball has been the turnovers, so there’s no need to lose sleep over Garland having an off shooting night.

 Rui Hachimura amassed 20 points (7-of-10 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, one assist, one steal, one block and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Jazz.
 After scoring 24 points on 7-of-24 shooting in his previous three games, Hachimura needed a night like Tuesday, even if the Clippers were on the wrong end of a blowout. This was Hachimura’s second game this season with at least 20 points, five rebounds and five assists. Even better for fantasy managers was his 70 percent shooting from the field, a strong output for a player shooting 41.5 percent on the season.
